newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to free general jailed for arms fraud.
newsitem.headline: Israel to free general jailed for arms fraud.

text.p: Israel plans to release from prison a former air force general who has served only half of a 13-year sentence for his part in a multi-million dollar arms purchasing scandal involving U.S. contracts.

"The prisoner will be released from jail on April 21 after serving half his term. That was the decision of the committee overseeing terms of his sentence," an army spokesman told Reuters on Sunday of prisoner Rami Dotan.

The committee said its main consideration was a ruling by doctors that Dotan was chronically ill and continued imprisonment could pose a danger to his life. It did not elaborate on the nature of his illness.
The decision drew widespread public outrage in Israel.

"This is an international disgrace. I don't understand the decision and I don't understand what kind of example we're providing the people of Israel," Israeli Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani told Israel Radio.

Dotan, former air force procurement chief, pled guilty before an Israeli court in 1991 to 12 counts including fraud, bribe-taking and breach of trust in connection with phoney arms purchases from the United States, Israel's main arms supplier.
He was sentenced to 13 years in prison and five years probation, reduced in rank to private, and agreed to return the $10 million dollars he defrauded from the defence ministry.
The affair shocked the Israeli public and raised questions about accountability in the military. Many public figures criticised the plea bargain as too lenient.
